newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Sept 11.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Sept 11.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) said late on Tuesday the positioning of its debt issues in offshore and domestic capital markets had been enhanced by the ratings upgrade by agency Standard & Poor's. It said on Tuesday it planned a medium-term note issue of unspecified size in the United States later this week. S&P also upgraded Westpac.
Twentieth Century Fox studios Tuesday said it plans to release its popular summer film "Independence Day" on videotape on November 22, just in time for the holidays.

Novus Petroleum Ltd said late on Tuesday it was on track to meet its prospectus forecast for a full year after tax profit of A$19.9 million before abnormals. Earlier, Novus reported a net profit after abnormals of A$8.94 million for the six months to June 30, up from A$3.04 million in the previous corresponding period.

Leighton Holdings Ltd chief executive Wal King said on Tuesday that the company would make an announcement soon, but he would not give any further details. "We're going to announce something in the next couple of days," King told Reuters when asked about the sharp rise in Leighton share price to a fresh high of A$5.60 earlier on Tuesday.

Gold and copper miner Straits Resources Ltd said on Wednesday it had agreed to buy Singapore's Straits Sebuku Pte Ltd for US$20.6 million. "The acquisition price of US$20.6 million will be funded in cash (US$10.6 million) from the company's reserves plus 7.91 million Straits Resources shares at A$1.60 per share," Straits said, adding it expected the deal would double its projected cashflow and revenue.
Hamilton Island posted a net loss of A$53.66 million for the year to June 30, 1996 early on Wednesday, compared with a profit of A$4.79 million in 1994/95.

Financial services group ING said on Tuesday its Australian unit Mercantile Mutual had sealed the takeover of funds manager Pacific Mutual Australia Limited for A$98 million (some 132 million guilders). "Mercantile Mutual...has unconditionally confirmed its bid for the shares of Pacific Mutual Australia Limited now that more than 90 percent of the shares have been tendered," ING said.
Leisure group due to release results for year to June 30.
